name: Munich
tagline: Beer gardens, palaces and the Alps on the horizon
summary: Bavaria's capital mixes royal palaces, world-class museums and the huge English Garden with beer halls and leafy beer gardens. It is the base for day trips to Neuschwanstein, the Alps and Salzburg, and every autumn it hosts Oktoberfest.
seasonNote: May to September is beer-garden season. Oktoberfest runs from mid-September to the first Sunday in October, when hotel prices double. December brings Christmas markets; January to March is cold and grey.
arrival: Munich Airport is 40 minutes from the centre on the S1 or S8 train. Trains arrive at the Hauptbahnhof from Berlin (about 4 hours), Vienna (4 hours) and Zurich (3.5 hours).
gettingAround: U-Bahn, S-Bahn and trams cover the city; a day ticket is good value, and the old town is walkable.
cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere now, but some beer gardens and small bakeries still prefer cash.
foodTip: Weisswurst with sweet mustard and a pretzel before noon, roast pork knuckle, Obatzda cheese spread and a litre of beer.
buyTip: Beer steins, lederhosen and dirndls, gingerbread hearts and Christmas ornaments.

items.name: Marienplatz and New Town Hall
items.summary: The main square, dominated by the Gothic New Town Hall and its glockenspiel.
items.expect: The glockenspiel plays at 11 am and noon (and 5 pm in summer).
items.tip: Climb the tower of St Peter's Church next door for the best view of the square.
items.why: The heart of Munich since the Middle Ages.

items.name: Munich Residenz
items.summary: The vast palace of the Bavarian kings, with the Renaissance Antiquarium hall and the royal treasury.
items.expect: Plan at least two hours; the combined ticket includes the treasury.
items.tip: Take the free audio guide and don't miss the Antiquarium.

items.name: English Garden
items.summary: One of the world's largest city parks, with a Chinese tower beer garden and surfers on the Eisbach wave.
items.expect: Free and open all day; the Eisbach surfers are at the southern tip.
items.tip: Rent a bike and stop at the Chinese Tower beer garden.

items.name: Nymphenburg Palace
items.summary: The Wittelsbachs' summer palace, with a Baroque park, pavilions and a royal coach museum.
items.expect: The park is free; the palace and pavilions need a ticket.
items.tip: Visit the Amalienburg hunting lodge in the park.

items.name: Deutsches Museum
items.summary: One of the world's largest science and technology museums, from mines to aircraft.
items.expect: Huge; pick a few halls.
items.tip: Book online and arrive at opening.
items.why: Great for families and on rainy days.

items.name: Dachau Concentration Camp Memorial
items.summary: The first Nazi concentration camp, now a memorial and museum.
items.expect: Free entry; about 45 minutes by S-Bahn and bus; not suitable for young children.
items.tip: Take the guided tour or audio guide for context.

items.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
items.summary: The fairy-tale castle of King Ludwig II above an Alpine gorge.
items.expect: A full day trip; timed tickets sell out, so book ahead.
items.tip: Walk to Marienbrücke bridge for the classic view.

items.name: Hofbräuhaus beer hall
items.summary: The famous royal brewery hall with long tables, a brass band and litre mugs.
items.expect: Loud and touristy, but fun.
items.tip: Share a table; it's expected.

items.name: Weisswurst breakfast
items.summary: White veal sausages with sweet mustard and a pretzel, eaten before noon.
items.expect: Traditionally peeled, not eaten with the skin.
items.tip: Try it at the Viktualienmarkt food market.

items.name: Augustiner beer garden
items.summary: A huge chestnut-shaded beer garden where you can bring your own food.
items.expect: Self-service; open in good weather.
items.tip: Bring a picnic, buy the beer.
items.why: The best of Munich summer life.

name: Zurich
tagline: A lakeside old town with the Alps beyond
summary: Switzerland's largest city sits where the Limmat river leaves Lake Zurich. Its medieval old town of guild houses and church towers, lake swimming in summer and excellent museums make it an easy start to any Swiss trip, with Lucerne and the Rhine Falls close by.
seasonNote: June to September is warm, with swimming in the lake and the river. December has Christmas markets. Winter is grey in the city but good for day trips to ski resorts.
arrival: Zurich Airport is 10 minutes from the main station by train. Trains run from Munich (3.5 hours), Milan (3.5 hours) and Paris (4 hours).
gettingAround: Trams and trains run like clockwork; the Swiss Travel Pass covers most transport and museums.
cashTip: Cards and phone payments work almost everywhere; prices are in francs, though euros are sometimes accepted at a poor rate.
foodTip: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (veal in cream with rösti), cheese fondue, and Luxemburgerli macarons from Sprüngli.
buyTip: Swiss chocolate, watches, Swiss army knives and Freitag bags.
baseArea: Altstadt or near the main station

items.name: Grossmünster
items.summary: The twin-towered Romanesque church where the Swiss Reformation began.
items.expect: Free to enter; a small fee to climb the tower.
items.tip: Climb the Karl tower for views over the river and lake.

items.name: Fraumünster
items.summary: A church famous for its five stained-glass windows by Marc Chagall.
items.expect: A small entry fee with an audio guide.
items.tip: Come when the sun lights the choir windows.
items.why: Chagall's colours in a medieval church.

items.name: Old Town and Lindenhof
items.summary: Lanes of guild houses and fountains, and a quiet hilltop square above the river.
items.expect: All walkable; the fountain water is drinkable.
items.tip: Watch the chess players on Lindenhof.

items.name: Lake Zurich
items.summary: Clear lake waters with promenades, swimming baths and boat cruises.
items.expect: Summer lidos charge a small fee; boats are covered by the travel pass.
items.tip: Take a short lake boat to Rapperswil or swim at Seebad Utoquai.

items.name: Swiss National Museum
items.summary: A castle-like museum telling the story of Switzerland.
items.expect: Next to the main station.
items.tip: Start with the permanent history exhibition.
items.why: Understand the country in two hours.

items.name: Uetliberg
items.summary: Zurich's own mountain, with a lookout tower over the city, lake and Alps.
items.expect: 20 minutes by train, then a short walk up.
items.tip: Go at sunset on a clear day.
items.why: The best view of Zurich and the Alps.

items.name: Rhine Falls
items.summary: Europe's most powerful waterfall, with boats to a rock in the middle.
items.expect: About 50 minutes by train; boats run from spring to autumn.
items.tip: Take the boat to the central rock.

items.name: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
items.summary: Sliced veal in a creamy mushroom sauce with crisp rösti.
items.expect: Served in old guild-house restaurants.
items.tip: Try it at a traditional Zunfthaus.

items.name: Cheese fondue
items.summary: Melted cheese with bread, shared from one pot.
items.expect: Best in winter; some restaurants serve it all year.
items.tip: Don't drop your bread in the pot.

items.name: Sprüngli chocolates
items.summary: A historic confectioner famous for tiny Luxemburgerli macarons.
items.expect: Shop and café on Paradeplatz.
items.tip: Buy a small box of Luxemburgerli; they last only a few days.

name: Stockholm
summary: Stockholm spreads across islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic. Its medieval old town, the royal palace, the Vasa warship museum and the open-air Skansen sit within walking distance, and boats run out to thousands of islands in the archipelago.
seasonNote: June to August has long light evenings and the archipelago at its best; Midsummer (late June) is the big festival. December has Christmas markets and Lucia; winter days are short and dark.
arrival: Arlanda Airport is 20 minutes from the centre on the Arlanda Express train. Trains arrive from Copenhagen (about 5 hours) and Oslo (6 hours); overnight ferries come from Helsinki, Tallinn and Riga.
gettingAround: The metro (with art-filled stations), trams and island ferries share one ticket; much of the centre is walkable.
cashTip: Sweden is almost cashless; many places don't take cash at all, so bring a card.
foodTip: Meatballs with lingonberries, herring, shrimp sandwiches, and fika: coffee with a cinnamon bun.
buyTip: Scandinavian design, Dala horses, glassware and licorice.

items.name: Gamla stan
items.summary: The medieval old town of narrow lanes, ochre houses and the Stortorget square.
items.expect: Busy in summer; very pretty in the evening.
items.tip: Find Mårten Trotzigs gränd, the narrowest lane.

items.name: Vasa Museum
items.summary: A complete 17th-century warship that sank on its maiden voyage, raised from the sea.
items.expect: Very popular; book a time slot in summer.
items.tip: See the ship from several floors.

items.name: Skansen
items.summary: The world's first open-air museum, with old Swedish houses, crafts and Nordic animals.
items.expect: Large; allow half a day.
items.tip: Go on a summer evening for folk dancing.

items.name: Stockholm City Hall
items.summary: The brick tower and Golden Hall where the Nobel banquet is held.
items.expect: Guided tours only; the tower is a separate climb in summer.
items.tip: Climb the tower for a view over Gamla stan.

items.name: Royal Palace
items.summary: One of Europe's largest palaces, with state rooms, the treasury and the changing of the guard.
items.expect: The guard changes around midday.
items.tip: Time your visit for the changing of the guard.

items.name: Fotografiska
items.summary: A photography museum in an old customs house, with a top-floor café over the water.
items.expect: Open late most evenings.
items.tip: Stay for dinner or a drink with the view.

items.name: Stockholm archipelago
items.summary: Thousands of islands of red cottages, pine trees and swimming rocks.
items.expect: Boats run from the centre; summer has the most sailings.
items.tip: Take the boat to Vaxholm or Grinda for a day.

items.name: Swedish meatballs
items.summary: Meatballs with cream sauce, mashed potatoes, lingonberries and pickled cucumber.
items.expect: Classic in traditional restaurants.
items.tip: Try them at an old-style kvarterskrog.

items.name: Fika and cinnamon buns
items.summary: The Swedish coffee break with cinnamon or cardamom buns.
items.expect: Cafés everywhere.
items.tip: Try a cardamom bun too.

items.name: Östermalm Food Hall
items.summary: A grand food hall with seafood counters, herring and shrimp sandwiches.
items.expect: Lunch is busiest.
items.tip: Order a skagen shrimp toast.

name: Brussels
summary: Belgium's capital centres on the Grand-Place, perhaps Europe's most beautiful square. Around it are art nouveau houses, comic-strip murals, the Magritte Museum and the Atomium, with chocolate shops and beer cafés on every corner and Bruges an hour away by train.
seasonNote: April to September is mildest, but it rains all year. The Flower Carpet covers the Grand-Place in August of even-numbered years. December brings the Winter Wonders market.
arrival: Brussels Airport is 20 minutes from the centre by train. Eurostar arrives from London (2 hours) and high-speed trains from Paris (1.5 hours) and Amsterdam (2 hours) at Brussels-Midi.
gettingAround: The centre is walkable; the metro and trams cover the rest.
cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; carry a few euros for frites stands and toilets.
foodTip: Moules-frites, frites with mayonnaise from a stand, waffles, and hundreds of Belgian beers.
buyTip: Chocolate pralines, speculoos biscuits, lace, comic books and beer.

items.name: Grand-Place
items.summary: A square of gilded guildhalls and a Gothic town hall.
items.expect: Busy all day; lit up beautifully at night.
items.tip: Come back after dark.
items.why: One of the most beautiful squares in the world.

items.name: Manneken Pis
items.summary: The tiny bronze statue of a boy, often dressed in one of his 1,000 costumes.
items.expect: Smaller than you expect.
items.tip: Check his costume calendar online.
items.why: A Brussels joke you have to see.
flow: Check his costume of the day.

items.name: Royal Galleries of Saint-Hubert
items.summary: Elegant 19th-century glass-roofed shopping arcades.
items.expect: Chocolate shops, cafés and a cinema.
items.tip: Taste pralines at Neuhaus, which started here.
items.why: One of Europe's first shopping arcades.

items.name: Magritte Museum
items.summary: The largest collection of René Magritte's surreal paintings.
items.expect: Part of the Royal Museums of Fine Arts.
items.tip: Combine it with the Old Masters galleries next door.

items.name: Belgian Comic Strip Center
items.summary: A museum of comics in an art nouveau department store, from Tintin to the Smurfs.
items.expect: Then follow the comic murals painted around the city.
items.tip: Pick up the comic mural walking map.
items.why: Belgium is the home of Tintin.

items.name: Atomium
items.summary: A 102-metre steel model of an iron crystal from the 1958 World's Fair.
items.expect: Reached by metro; spheres hold exhibitions and a viewpoint.
items.tip: Go at opening to avoid queues for the lift.

items.name: Bruges
items.summary: A medieval canal town of brick gables, belfries and boat rides.
items.expect: An hour by train; very busy on summer weekends.
items.tip: Stay into the evening when the day-trippers leave.

items.name: Moules-frites
items.summary: A pot of mussels steamed in white wine or beer, with frites.
items.expect: Best in autumn and winter.
items.tip: Avoid the touts on Rue des Bouchers; try Sainte-Catherine.

items.name: Belgian waffles
items.summary: Crisp Brussels waffles or sweet, chewy Liège waffles from street stands.
items.expect: Locals eat them plain or with powdered sugar.
items.tip: Try a Liège waffle warm.

items.name: Belgian chocolate
items.summary: Pralines from master chocolatiers around the Sablon square.
items.expect: Many shops offer tastings.
items.tip: Compare Pierre Marcolini, Wittamer and Neuhaus.

name: Warsaw
tagline: A rebuilt old town and a city of stories
summary: Poland's capital was almost destroyed in 1944 and rebuilt brick by brick. Today its reconstructed Old Town is a World Heritage Site, and powerful museums tell the story of the Warsaw Uprising and Polish Jews, alongside royal palaces, Chopin concerts in the park and a lively food scene.
seasonNote: May to September is warm, with free Chopin concerts in Łazienki Park on summer Sundays. Winters are cold, with a Christmas market in the Old Town.
arrival: Chopin Airport is 25 minutes from the centre by train. Trains arrive from Kraków (2.5 hours), Berlin (5.5 hours) and Gdańsk (3 hours).
gettingAround: Metro, trams and buses share a ticket; the Royal Route links the main sights on foot.
cashTip: Cards and phone payments work almost everywhere, even at small stands.
foodTip: Pierogi, żurek sour rye soup, and cheap home cooking at a milk bar (bar mleczny).
buyTip: Amber jewellery, Bolesławiec pottery, vodka and Polish posters.
baseArea: Śródmieście near the Old Town or Nowy Świat

items.name: Old Town
items.summary: A colourful market square and lanes rebuilt after the war from old paintings and plans.
items.expect: Free to wander; the museum explains the rebuilding.
items.tip: Watch the short film on the rebuilding at the Warsaw Museum.
items.why: A World Heritage Site rebuilt from rubble.

items.name: Royal Castle
items.summary: The rebuilt home of Polish kings, with grand halls and paintings by Canaletto's nephew.
items.expect: Free entry on some days of the week.
items.tip: See the Canaletto Room's paintings of old Warsaw.

items.name: Warsaw Rising Museum
items.summary: An immersive museum of the 1944 uprising against Nazi occupation.
items.expect: Moving and intense; allow two to three hours.
items.tip: Watch the 3D film City of Ruins.

items.name: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews
items.wiki: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews
items.summary: A thousand years of Jewish life in Poland, in the former ghetto area.
items.expect: Allow three hours; the building itself is striking.
items.tip: Walk to the Ghetto Heroes Monument outside.

items.name: Łazienki Park
items.summary: A royal park with a palace on the water, peacocks and the Chopin monument.
items.expect: Free Chopin concerts at the monument on summer Sundays.
items.tip: Come on a Sunday from May to September.

items.name: Palace of Culture and Science
items.summary: Stalin's gift to Poland, with a 30th-floor viewing terrace.
items.expect: Lifts to the terrace run until late.
items.tip: Go at sunset.
items.why: Love it or hate it, it is Warsaw's landmark.
flow: Buy a ticket in the lobby.

items.name: Wilanów Palace
items.summary: A Baroque royal palace with formal gardens on the edge of the city.
items.expect: About 30 minutes by bus.
items.tip: Visit the gardens in spring and summer.
items.why: One of Poland's few palaces to survive the war.

items.name: Pierogi
items.summary: Dumplings filled with potato and cheese, meat, cabbage or fruit.
items.expect: Boiled or fried; served with onions and sour cream.
items.tip: Order a mixed plate to try several fillings.

items.name: Milk bar lunch
items.summary: Cheap canteens serving home-style Polish cooking since communist times.
items.expect: Order at the counter; menus may be Polish only.
items.tip: Point and smile; try the tomato soup.
items.why: Real local food at low prices.

items.name: Żurek soup
items.summary: A sour rye soup with sausage and egg, sometimes served in a bread bowl.
items.expect: Warming in winter.
items.tip: Try it in a bread bowl once.

name: Heraklion
summary: Crete's capital is a busy port city behind Venetian walls. Just outside it lies Knossos, the palace of the Minoans, Europe's first great civilisation, and its archaeological museum holds their finest treasures. It's the base for central and eastern Crete's beaches, gorges and villages.
seasonNote: May, June, September and October are warm without the crowds and heat of July and August. Winter is mild but many beach places close.
arrival: Heraklion Airport is 15 minutes from the centre. Ferries arrive from Athens (Piraeus, 7 to 9 hours overnight) and Santorini (about 2 hours).
gettingAround: City buses run to Knossos; rent a car to explore the island.
cashTip: Cards work in most places; carry cash for village tavernas and kiosks.
foodTip: Dakos (barley rusk with tomato and feta), snails, lamb with greens, and a free shot of raki after dinner.
buyTip: Cretan olive oil, thyme honey, raki and handmade knives.
baseArea: Old town near the Lions Square

connections.note: Fast ferries from spring to autumn.

items.name: Knossos
items.summary: The vast Bronze Age palace of the Minoans, partly restored with red columns and frescoes.
items.expect: Little shade; go early and bring water.
items.tip: Hire a guide at the gate to understand the ruins.

items.name: Heraklion Archaeological Museum
items.summary: The world's finest Minoan collection: the Phaistos Disc, snake goddesses and the bull-leaping fresco.
items.expect: Best after visiting Knossos.
items.tip: Visit the fresco rooms upstairs.

items.name: Koules Fortress
items.summary: A Venetian sea fortress guarding the old harbour.
items.expect: Walk along the breakwater at sunset.
items.tip: Climb to the rooftop for harbour views.

items.name: Lions Square and old town
items.summary: A Venetian lion fountain, the loggia and lively streets of cafés and markets.
items.expect: Busy and local, especially in the evening.
items.tip: Walk down 1866 Street market.
items.why: The everyday heart of the city.

items.name: Phaistos
items.summary: A second Minoan palace on a hill over the Messara plain, less restored than Knossos.
items.expect: About 1 hour 15 minutes by car.
items.tip: Combine with Matala beach and its caves.
items.why: Quieter Minoan ruins with huge views.

items.name: Cretaquarium
items.summary: One of Europe's largest aquariums, showing Mediterranean sea life.
items.expect: 20 minutes by car east of the city.
items.tip: Good for families on a hot afternoon.

items.name: Spinalonga
items.summary: A Venetian island fortress that later became a leper colony.
items.expect: About 1 hour by car, then a short boat from Elounda or Plaka.
items.tip: Read or watch The Island first.

items.name: Dakos
items.summary: A barley rusk soaked with tomato, olive oil, feta or mizithra cheese and oregano.
items.expect: On every taverna menu.
items.tip: Pair it with a plate of snails.

items.name: Raki and mezedes
items.summary: Strong grape spirit served with small plates of cheese, olives and pies.
items.expect: Often offered free after dinner.
items.tip: Say yes to the second round, slowly.

items.name: Bougatsa
items.summary: Flaky pastry filled with cream or sweet cheese, dusted with sugar and cinnamon.
items.expect: A morning treat.
items.tip: Order the cheese version, Heraklion-style.

name: Rhodes
tagline: A knights' walled city in the Aegean sun
summary: Rhodes Town wraps one of Europe's best-preserved medieval cities, built by the Knights of St John, inside massive walls. Beyond it the island has beaches, the white village of Lindos below its acropolis, and boats to nearby Symi.
seasonNote: May, June, September and October are ideal. July and August are hot and crowded. In winter many hotels close.
arrival: Rhodes Airport is 25 minutes from town. Flights come from Athens (1 hour) and many European cities in summer; ferries run from Piraeus (about 13 hours) and nearby islands.
gettingAround: The old town is car-free; buses run to Lindos and beaches, or rent a car or scooter.
cashTip: Cards are widely accepted; keep cash for small tavernas and beach sunbeds.
foodTip: Grilled fish, souvlaki, Greek salad with island cheese, and pitaroudia chickpea fritters.
buyTip: Local honey, olive-oil soap, ceramics from Lindos and leather sandals.
baseArea: Inside the old town walls or near Mandraki

connections.note: Long ferries also run from Piraeus.
Seasonal; or a ferry to Marmaris in Türkiye.

items.name: Medieval City
items.summary: Cobbled lanes, gates and towers inside 4 km of walls built by the Knights of St John.
items.expect: Free to wander; walls walks open on some days.
items.tip: Get lost in the back lanes away from Socratous Street.

items.name: Palace of the Grand Master
items.wiki: Palace of the Grand Master of the Knights of Rhodes
items.summary: The knights' fortress-palace, with mosaic floors from Kos.
items.expect: Combined tickets include other old town sites.
items.tip: Go at opening before cruise groups.
items.why: The seat of the Knights of St John.

items.name: Street of the Knights
items.summary: A perfect medieval street of the knights' inns, each built by a different nation.
items.expect: Short and beautiful, especially at dusk.
items.tip: Look for the coats of arms above the doors.

items.name: Archaeological Museum of Rhodes
items.summary: Classical statues and finds in the knights' hospital.
items.expect: A quiet garden in the courtyard.
items.tip: Find the Aphrodite of Rhodes.
items.why: Ancient Rhodes in a medieval building.

items.name: Mandraki Harbour
items.summary: The old harbour where the Colossus once stood, now marked by deer statues and windmills.
items.expect: Boats to Symi and beaches leave here.
items.tip: Walk out to the windmills and St Nicholas fortress.
items.why: Where one of the Seven Wonders stood.

items.name: Lindos
items.summary: A white village below an acropolis with a Doric temple above the sea.
items.expect: About an hour by car or bus; the climb is hot and steep.
items.tip: Go early or late, and swim at St Paul's Bay.

items.name: Symi
items.summary: A neighbouring island with a harbour of pastel neoclassical houses.
items.expect: Day boats from Mandraki take about 1 to 2 hours.
items.tip: Stay for lunch at the harbour.
items.why: The prettiest harbour in the Dodecanese.

items.name: Souvlaki and gyros
items.summary: Grilled meat skewers or gyros in pita with tomato, onion and tzatziki.
items.expect: Cheap and everywhere.
items.tip: Eat where locals queue.

items.name: Grilled fish taverna
items.summary: Fresh fish grilled simply with lemon and olive oil, priced by weight.
items.expect: Ask the price before ordering.
items.tip: Pick your fish from the counter.

items.name: Pitaroudia and mezedes
items.summary: Chickpea or tomato fritters and small plates to share with ouzo.
items.expect: A Rhodes speciality.
items.tip: Order several mezedes for the table.
items.why: The local taste of the island.
